title: 1978 AHSME Problem 12
statement: In \(\triangle ADE,\) \(\angle ADE=140^\circ,\) points \(B\) and \(C\) lie on sides \(AD\) and \(AE,\) respectively, and points \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) \(D,\) \(E\) are distinct. If lengths \(AB,\) \(BC,\) \(CD,\) and \(DE\) are all equal, then the measure of \(\angle EAD\) is

solutions.text:
Let \(x=\angle BAC=\angle BCA,\) \(y=\angle CBD=\angle CDB,\) and \(z=\angle DCE=\angle DEC.\) The exterior-angle theorem applied successively gives \[ y=2x,\qquad z=x+y=3x. \] The angles of \(\triangle ADE\) are \(x,\) \(140^\circ,\) and \(z,\) so \(x+140^\circ+3x=180^\circ.\) Hence \(x=10^\circ.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Name \(\angle BAC=\angle BCA=x\) and use the successive isosceles triangles
Express the other base angles in terms of \(x,\) then use the angle sum in \(\triangle ADE\)
